programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Alan Alda (5/19/81)
programme.desc: M*A*S*H* star Alan Alda discusses his career and the impact of celebrity on his life. Comedian David Brenner riffs on health food, controlling his weight and eating in New York.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Bo Derek (7/24/81)
programme.desc: TV star Michael Landon gets sentimental over Bonanza; watching episodes dubbed in Japanese and promoting the show at county fairs. Actress Bo Derek talks about vine-swinging for Tarzan, the Ape Man.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Angie Dickinson (7/31/81)
programme.desc: Show biz veteran Angie Dickinson talks about men who whistle at women, Tommy Lasorda chats about losing weight, and Dom DeLuise dishes on doing an off-Broadway play with Barbra Streisand.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - John Travolta (8/6/81)
programme.desc: Actor/pilot John Travolta on flying lessons, dropping out of high school and getting his first part. Humorist Erma Bombeck complains that "housewives" on commercials don't look like housewives.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - John Travolta (8/6/81)

programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Burt Reynolds (2/11/82)

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Roger Moore (3/30/82)
programme.desc: With five Bond movies under his belt, Sir Roger Moore says he'll keep going. Having just won the Oscar for Reds, Maureen Stapleton wonders aloud how it will impact her career.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Jodie Foster (3/4/83)
programme.desc: Yale student and movie star Jodie Foster chats about college life, John Hinckley and working with Peter O'Toole. Tim Conway describes the brochure he asks his prospective dates to read.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Donald Sutherland (5/13/83)
programme.desc: Autograph hounds watch out: Donald Sutherland has a policy on handling signature seekers. Comic actor Martin Mull answers his fan mail and shows off his artwork.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Cloris Leachman (5/9/84)
programme.desc: Eight-time Emmy winner Cloris Leachman reveals her favorite prize --mother of the year -- awarded by a club in New York. 91year old Olympic athlete Abel Kivat discusses how he keeps in shape.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Miss Piggy (7/12/84)
programme.desc: The epitome of beauty and elegance, Miss Piggy extols the joys of learning French. Comedian Howie Mandel covers his seat with plastic because he says he wants to feel like he's at his mom's.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Peter Fonda (1/4/85)
programme.desc: Actor/screenwriter Peter Fonda opens up about being compared to his father and sister. Charles Nelson Reilly recalls his dad pouring cheap bourbon into fancy bottles to hide their poverty.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Peter Fonda (1/4/85)

programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Angie Dickinson (1/2/86)

programme.desc: The always virile Burt Reynolds reflects on his 1973 Cosmo poster, and his five-year romance with actress Loni Anderson. The maturing boy-toy-turned-movie-star is penning his autobiography.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - George C. Scott (11/3/87)
programme.desc: The first actor to refuse an Oscar, George C. Scott for the title role in Patton, chats about his love of theatre, the many bombs in which he's appeared and turning 60 years old.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - Burt Reynolds (2/25/88)
programme.desc: Taking up the pen, Burt Reynolds discusses his work on his autobiography. He comments on his streak of box office flops. Burt warmly welcomes Eddy Edwards, Britain's one-man Olympic Ski Jumping team.

programme.title: The Johnny Carson Show
programme.sub-title: The Johnny Carson Show: Hollywood Icons Of The '70s - George Segal (11/8/91)
programme.desc: Oscar nom'd George Segal demonstrates playing an old man using prosthetics, glasses and gait. Comedian Drew Carey riffs on his high school reunion, driving a Yugo and his love of bad food.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.sub-title: The Study of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Viewing a multifaceted image of Renaissance Italy that explains why the period remains fundamental to Western culture; lectures on city-states are interspersed with those on philosophy, education and other cultural elements relevant to Italy.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: The Renaissance becomes visible at different times in different places; it is the first self-conscious period of European history, articulated by the Humanist writer Giovanni Boccaccio; he recognizes that a new world is being created.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: The Renaissance develops because of the unique circumstances of the Italian peninsula; urban life remains strong; a lay tradition of study and secular values is sustained; memories of the Roman Empire are everywhere.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.sub-title: The Age of Dante-Guelfs and Ghibellines
programme.desc: The Florentine poet Dante defines the transition from the medieval to the Renaissance; he is born into a period of dispute between the Guelphs and the Ghibellines; the Guelf victory in Florence helps set the stage for the Renaissance.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.sub-title: Petrarch and the Foundations of Humanism
programme.desc: Francesco Petrarca can be described as the father of Humanism; his love of Latin classics and early Christian thinkers drives him to investigate his own motivations and feelings; his desire to know himself recovers the autobiography genre.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: For Italians, ancient Rome is their national history; this rich tradition is increasingly regarded as an intellectual heritage to be mined for contemporary use, so its wisdom can be applied to the circumstances of 14th-century Italy.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Florence is the cradle of the Renaissance; by the mid-13th century, huge fortunes are being made by men whose families emigrate from the countryside; these wealthy merchants are largely excluded from government; a bourgeois revolution in 1293.

programme.title: The Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Florence's now-dominant mercantile classes are attracted to the ideals of ancient Rome; Romans are, after all, like them; urban, cosmopolitan and secular; civic humanism; the citizen's responsibility to the community becomes a powerful ethic.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Examining the features of late medieval culture in Italy that pave the way for the Renaissance; in painting, Giotto di Bondone evolves a proto-Renaissance style in contrast to the prevailing late-Gothic style.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Around 1400, a European-wide style known as International Gothic flourishes in Italy; artists including Lorenzo Monaco and Gentile da Fabriano retain the style; others, such as Lorenzo Ghiberti, develop a new style that is known as Renaissance.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Architecture is central to understanding the birth of the Renaissance; it is in Florence that the first great buildings of the Renaissance are constructed; looking at the buildings of Filippo Brunelleschi and the bronze doors of Lorenzo Ghiberti.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Donatello is a key Italian artist of the 15th century; tracing Donatello's work until he moves to Padua in 1443; Luca della Robbia's choir gallery for the Florence Cathedral is in direct competition with Donatello's choir gallery for the same church.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: The first of two lectures on Masaccio examines his "Pisa Altarpiece"; studying Masaccio's monumental fresco "The Trinity", with attention to his introduction of one-point perspective.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Studying Masaccio's principal frescoes for the Brancacci Chapel, with special attention to their melding of style and narrative content; Masaccio undertakes the project with Masolino.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.sub-title: Fra Angelico and Fra Filippo Lippi
programme.desc: Fra Angelico and Fra Filippo Lippi are leading painters in Florence after Masaccio's death; Fra Angelico switches between a late medieval style and a more realistic Renaissance manner; Fra Filippo Lippi's paintings combine charm and inward quietness.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Paintings by three contrasting artists in Florence; Paolo Uccello is devoted to foreshortening; Andrea del Castagno finds ways to make figures look like painted sculptures; Domenico Veneziano introduces a tonal delicacy and pastel palette.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.desc: Surveying the geography, cultures and time span to be covered; discussing the organization of a study and its key concepts; learning and understanding important places, civilizations and events in Mesoamerica.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.desc: The Olmecs at the dawn of the Mesoamerican civilization; how the Olmecs represent one of only six cradles of early civilization in world history; how they were discovered; investigating three sites where they lived.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.sub-title: Olmec Art as the Mother Culture
programme.desc: Delving into Olmec art; searching for clues about who the Olmecs were and what preoccupied them; the mysteries of giant sculpted heads, jaguar carvings and full-bearded figures depicting men who some think were foreigners.

programme.title: Maya to Aztec: Ancient Mesoamerica Revealed
programme.desc: Investigating other cultures that thrived in Mesoamerica at the time of the Olmecs, such as the Zapotecs in the Oaxaca Valley; probing intriguing archeological evidence that raises the question of who influenced whom.
